explain.say: A moving car carries movement energy. Ordinary brakes turn all of it into heat, which is wasted. Regenerative braking captures much of it and stores it back in the battery.

faq.q: How much energy does regenerative braking save?
faq.a: In a typical stop roughly half to two thirds of the movement energy goes back into the battery. Over a town journey that can stretch the range noticeably.

faq.q: How does a motor become a generator?
faq.a: An electric motor and a generator are the same machine used two ways. Push current through it and it turns; turn it with the wheels and current flows out.

faq.q: Why do electric cars still have normal brakes?
faq.a: Regenerative braking cannot stop the car hard enough in an emergency, works poorly at very low speed and is limited when the battery is full or very cold. Friction brakes cover those times.
asks: Do electric cars have brake pads?

faq.q: Why does an electric car slow down when I lift off the pedal?
faq.a: Lifting off switches the motor to generating, which takes energy from the car and slows it. When this is strong enough to bring the car to a stop, it is called one-pedal driving.

faq.q: Do brake pads last longer on electric cars?
faq.a: Yes. Because regenerative braking does most of the slowing, the friction brakes are used much less, so pads and discs can last far longer.

facts: Regenerative braking uses the drive motor as a generator.
Formula 1 introduced braking energy recovery, called KERS, in 2009.
Brake pads on electric cars often last much longer because regenerative braking does much of the work.
